## 10. Critical pointers (easy to get wrong)

- **`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`.** Orchestrator pipeline executions live in `pipeline_runs`; DQ suite executions live in `runs`. They link via `triggered_by: '<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>'`.
- **`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic.** Composite key (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. Don't add an ADF-specific bindings table.
- **PII redaction at the logger level**, not at every call site. The redactor sits in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** Code that depends on a new column ships in a separate PR *after* the migration is deployed.
- **The Week-3 threshold migration already added the schema seams (done).** It landed `check.kind` (default `'expectation'`), `results.metric_value` (NUMERIC) + `duration_ms` (INT), and the severity thresholds — see ADR `0012`. `metric_value` is the SQL-aggregatable scalar a monitor measured; **don't store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`** (you can't `AVG()`/`STDDEV()` it for trends or anomaly baselines), and **don't add a second migration re-introducing these columns**.
- **Secret scanning in pre-commit AND CI.** Don't rely on one alone.
- **Azure Monitor alert setup (Week 7) needs the deployed public API URL.** Deployment must come first; coordinate Container Apps ingress with infra/security before Week 7 to avoid a deployment-day surprise.
- **MCP tool descriptions are LLM-facing, not REST-API-facing.** Write them for natural-language selection; test against the 4 canonical NL queries in the roadmap.

## 11. What NOT to do

- ❌ Don't add ADF or Airflow as a queryable datasource in the connection editor / check editor / suite model.
- ❌ Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
- ❌ Don't deepen Azure lock-in: no reading Entra/OIDC provider claims in route/service code (depend on the generic `get_current_user`), no hardcoded Azure resource names/endpoints in business logic, no Azure-only assumptions baked into container images. Azure is one impl behind each seam — see ADR [0010](docs/site/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) / [0013](docs/site/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md).
- ❌ Don't `git commit --no-verify` past hooks. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
- ❌ Don't commit `.env` files. Use `.env.example` / `.env.app.example` as the templates.
- ❌ Don't put a credential — **even a local/mock one** — in any git-tracked file (templates, `scripts/`, CI, compose). Env templates ship the secret keys **blank** with the shape in a comment; `scripts/setup.sh` generates the local-dev password into the gitignored `.env`/`.env.app` on first run. Non-secret config defaults and non-secret identifiers (db/user name) may stay populated.
- ❌ Don't drop columns in the same PR as the code change that stops using them. Two-step it.
- ❌ Don't fix bugs silently. Raise a GitHub issue, then PR with `Fixes #N`.
- ❌ **Don't dismiss a finding because it's pre-existing.** DataQ is in production — a defect that predates your change is live for users right now, so its age is irrelevant to whether it matters. Every finding ends **fixed or filed**, never "noted in a review reply" or "documented in a docstring" (CONTRIBUTING rule 3a). Concluding it is genuinely not a defect is fine, but record the determination and evidence — verified-benign is a valid outcome, unexamined is not.
- ❌ Don't batch unrelated changes into one commit. One functionality per commit.
- ❌ Don't track GX Core at "latest." Pin the version in `environment.yml` — GX v1 API has drifted across point releases.
- ❌ Don't add a dependency under a strong-copyleft or source-available license (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL/Elastic, Commons-Clause) — DataQ ships MIT (ADR [0031](docs/site/adr/0031-oss-byol-distribution-licensing.md), CONTRIBUTING rule 40); weak copyleft (LGPL/MPL) is OK with notices. Exceptions need an ADR.
- ❌ Don't use venv or poetry for backend dev. Conda only.
- ❌ Don't write the MCP layer before Week 7. The service layer must stabilise first.

Verified-good: single public surface both clouds, api unreachable directly (Azure 404 / AWS ALB network-denied + origin secret), ECS task public IPs inbound-blocked, RDS private+encrypted, rate limiting live and enforcing (150-burst → 429 on both), docs off in prod, webhooks HMAC/constant-time. **#1386 was live-exploitable:** the Cognito pool had `AllowAdminCreateUserOnly: false` and its hosted UI served a working signup form, while the generic-OIDC path had **no app-side allowlist** — `_upsert_user` provisions an account for any token the issuer vouches for, so the IdP's registration policy silently WAS the product's access policy: anyone on the internet could self-register into the workspace. That also dissolved the *single-tenant, workspace-trusted* premise #1118 is deliberately accepted under, turning a known internal credential-exfiltration risk into a remotely reachable one. Fixed at the IdP (`allow_admin_create_user_only`) **and** in the app (`OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`/`_DOMAINS`, checked per-request so it revokes as well as admits; empty stays open by design — fail-closed would lock a workspace out on a routine image bump — but logs `auth_oidc_no_signup_allowlist` at WARNING). **/code-review then caught the fix's own blind spot: a THIRD generic-OIDC resolver.** Unifying the two REST dependencies was not enough — `mcp/auth.py`'s `resolve_current_user` called `_upsert_user` directly, so a token the REST API 403s authenticated at `/mcp` and got all 8 tools incl. `trigger_suite_run`, breaking the invariant that file's own Azure-guest branch states out loud. **#1387:** ZERO security response headers on either cloud (repo-wide grep found none defined anywhere). The trap: nginx drops inherited `add_header` at any level declaring its own, and three locations set `Cache-Control` — including `location /`, which serves index.html — so a server-level block would have been silently absent from exactly the response that needs a CSP, while looking correct in the config. **Proven, not assumed:** removing the `location /` re-include drops index.html to 0 headers with the server-level include still present. CSP `connect-src` is a separate runtime var, NOT derived from `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` — an authority carries a path, CSP matches by path prefix, and Azure AD's token endpoint sits outside it; live AWS confirmed the same shape from the other direction (token endpoint `…auth.us-east-2.amazoncognito.com` is a DIFFERENT host from JWKS `cognito-idp…`, so Cognito needs BOTH). Image default is `https:` not empty, so a BYO upgrade can't silently break sign-in. **#1388:** CloudFront ran `CachingDisabled` on every path — a pure pass-through absorbing nothing — in front of an in-app limiter that **fails open**, i.e. the pressure most likely to hurt Redis is what disables it. Added a WAF per-IP ceiling (2000/5min) + an 8KB body cap (import path scoped out: a WAF block happens at the edge, so its false positive has no origin log at all) and extension-matched `/assets/*.<ext>` edge caching — **not** the `/assets/*` prefix, which review caught would re-collide with the SPA's own `/assets/:assetId` route (#802 class). **Deployed to both clouds on `92c97b8c`** — Azure [run 31933670333](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31933670333) + AWS [run 31933647024](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31933647024), both green. A test states that as an invariant rather than leaving the empty admin sweep looking like a forgotten row.

**The RBAC ask produced the structural change worth carrying forward: the tool-surface tripwire became DATA.** `server._require_role` is the MCP twin of the FastAPI-only `core.auth.require_role` — it cannot *be* that function, but both resolve through the same `core.roles.resolve_role` and rank with the same `ROLE_RANK`, which is exactly what keeping `core/roles.py` FastAPI-free was for. More importantly, `tests/support/mcp_gates.GATES` now declares each tool's **actual** gate and four sweeps are driven off it (Viewer-denied, Member-denied, outsider-denied, and a guard that `read` tools genuinely take no `suite_id`). The old bare set of names caught a tool being *added* but not one added with the **wrong** gate — a name in the wrong comment group looks identical to a name in the right one — and it immediately caught `profile_column` filed under "read-only" while gating on `edit`. Declaring the gate means adding a row is adding a test.

**The four `/code-review` passes returned 19 findings, and almost none were crashes — they were *honesty* defects, which is the failure mode this surface has and the REST API does not.** The same shape recurred six times: a value that is literally true and misleading to a reader with no UI around it. An expired snooze returned raw reads as active suppression on the one question ("why was there no alert?") where a wrong answer is most confident. A mid-run suite's partial outcome (`3/3, worst_severity: null`) is precisely the tool's own definition of "nothing failed", asserted about a run that has barely started — the REST runs table survives it only because a "running" badge sits beside the numbers; **an LLM has no badge, it has whatever fields it is handed**. `consecutive_run_failures: 0` renders *unknown* as a fact. A null `credential_expires_at` conflated "no readable lifetime" with "never looked". `has_email_recipients` was derived from `EMAIL_TO` while delivery also needs the SMTP transport. And `get_notification_config` reported only the per-suite webhook, so the commonest deployment shape — one workspace webhook, no overrides — answered "who gets told when orders fails?" with **nobody**. Every gate in both batches was then mutation-verified by removing it and confirming the sweep goes red; one mutation additionally proved the tool *executed* for an unauthorized user (a `check_restored` log line), which is what distinguishes "fails" from "fails for the right reason".

**Shipped 2026-08-17 — the MCP honesty pass, all 46 tools ([#1444](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1444), user-directed).** The directive: *"The UI is expected that user will know the details. But in the MCP, that is not applicable… the answers should give the limitation and mention what it cannot see clearly to the user."* The UI's **human** supplies the missing context for free — the row count, the timestamps, the "running" badge, the filter they themselves chose. An LLM has the fields it is handed and the docstring, so a tool returning literally-true values while omitting its blind spot produces a *confident wrong answer*, which is worse than an error.

**Audited all 46 against six criteria** — population (what an empty result does NOT prove) · time window · truncation (detectable from DATA, not length) · freshness · null/zero semantics · adjacent blindness. ~75 findings. **Six docstrings were not thin but FALSE:** `get_health_score` promised "a per-day trend of the score" over a per-day count of *runs* by lifecycle status (no daily score exists); `test_connection` promised a "classified failure reason" the code deliberately withholds; `snooze_check` read as a per-check mute when suppression is per **run**; `delete_check`'s cascade omitted incidents (`Incident.check_id` is CASCADE, so it erases an open one); `trigger_suite_run` said "run the orders suite on DEV" with no env parameter; `list_connections`' `consecutive_run_failures` is the **minimum** streak across suites and reads 0 unless *every* suite is failing.

**Where a limit could be a field it became one** — prose is skippable, a field the model must branch on is not: `redaction`/`redacted_columns` (REST has had them since #1115; MCP dropped them, so a masked sample was indistinguishable from an unmasked one), `results_final`, `truncated` + `oldest_in_page`/`newest_in_page`, `sampled`/`sample_row_limit` (ADLS/S3/Iceberg profile ≤100k rows, so `row_count` was the *sample* size stated as the table's), `runnable: false`, `prior_incident_id`.

**Three lessons, all from verification catching me rather than me catching the code.** (1) A rendered-catalog check found four docstrings my *source-level* scan called clean — the splices were mid-sentence, visible only in the assembled description. (2) A routing re-run then found my repair had **corrupted two descriptions**, because my duplicate detector matched adjacent identical *words* and a repeated *phrase* walked through it — and the `list_checks` corruption sat on a safety caveat. (3) The same re-run found I had **overcorrected on ordering**: five tools led with a bolded warning, pushing the "Returns…" contract below it, which makes *selection* harder without making the caveat more likely to be read. Standing shape: **summary → what it returns → caveats.** Measured effect after the fixes: the disclosures changed the answer on **12 of 15** requests and prevented four confident wrong ones.

**And the review caught the pass's own failure mode.** I had written "**this tool can only ever ADD masking**" on `set_column_policy` — a confident absolute the code does not support, since a column named as `identifier_column` is shown unless it affirmatively classifies as PII. A false safety guarantee, produced by the very exercise meant to remove them. **The lifecycle docstrings carry the load here, because both verbs are about the *incident*, not the data.** Acknowledging changes nothing and does **not** stop alerts — the check still runs, still fails, still notifies — so it points at `snooze_check` for what the user probably meant. Resolving re-runs nothing and fixes nothing: if the problem is still there the next failing run opens a **new** incident (a resolved one is never reopened), so the docstring steers toward `trigger_suite_run` to confirm before declaring victory. Both refuse the closed-state transition rather than silently no-opping, which would let an assistant report an action that never happened.

Fixed by adding that exact phrase — not a loose word like "requires", since anything also matching an argument-validation message would let a gateless tool pass by failing for the wrong reason. **Two scoping rules had to reach the docstrings, not just the code.** The asset rollup is **workspace-true** (ADR 0037) — `list_visible_assets` takes no user and aggregates over ALL composing suites — so a model handed the number with no caveat will describe it as covering what the caller can see; `get_asset` therefore reports `restricted_suite_count` beside the grant-filtered suite list. Incidents, by the same ADR, stay **behind suite grants**: they are itemized failure evidence, not identity, so `get_incident` is 404-no-leak. That second rule is why **`incident:view` is a new gate value** rather than `suite:view` — the tool takes an *incident* id, so the sweep must materialise a real incident on the probe suite; a fabricated id raises "incident not found", which is in the accepted-denial vocabulary, and the sweep would pass **with the gate deleted**. The same vacuous-pass shape as `_REAL_RUN` / `_REAL_CHECK` / the 3A `CheckVersion` trap, hit for the fourth time. Both new gates were mutation-verified.

**The 404-no-leak rule moved out of the HTTP layer** into `incident_service.load_visible_incident`, shared by REST and MCP. A second hand-written copy of the only thing standing between an incident's evidence and an ungranted caller is the "guard at one door and not its sibling" shape, and that divergence is invisible until it leaks. Three honesty fields exist because the raw value is true and misleading alone — `monitored` (an unmonitored asset reads as a clean bill of health), `truncated` (against the real total; `len(page) == limit` is wrong on the exact-boundary page), and `lineage.qualified_by` (an empty graph behind a failing poller must never read as "nothing feeds this table" — #828). **Unplanned, user-directed, shipped 2026-08-16 — the ADR [0033](docs/site/adr/0033-workspace-roles-rbac.md) workspace-roles (RBAC) track, picked up from the `v1.1 Backlog`** (umbrella [#744](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/744), now closed): **five PRs** ([#1396](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1396)–[#1400](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1400)) taking all four slices plus the [#1118](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118) class W5 had deferred *specifically* to this track. Authorization is now genuinely two axes: a stored **`users.role`** (`admin | member | viewer`) beside the per-suite `view/edit/admin/owner` ladder, both enforced on REST and MCP, both resolving **per request** — so a demotion lands on the target's next call, *including calls made with PATs they already hold*, with no token to revoke. `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` demotes to a **bootstrap seed + lockout break-glass** that only ever grants. **This closes gap G-e and the standing hole where any authenticated user — even one holding a single `view` share — could delete or re-credential the connection every suite in the workspace ran on** (⚠️ breaking for Members who managed connections; promote before upgrading, CHANGELOG carries the note). Roles are managed in **Admin → Members** behind a **last-admin guard that counts stored-role admins only** (an allowlist-resolved admin can vanish with the next deploy) under `FOR UPDATE`, with a structured audit line per change — the durable audit *table* stays ADR 0020's deferred #310.

**The reviews caught five things the design did not, and they share one shape — a rule that was stated but not enforced, or enforced in one place but not its sibling:** (1) a **third door** around the new gates — `POST /_probe/snowflake-suite` creates a Connection *and* a Suite and was ungated; the gates went on the resources' own routes and a sibling endpoint creating the same resources by another name was invisible to that reasoning; (2) the **last-admin guard was bypassable**, reading `previous` before taking the lock so a stale value skipped the check entirely and could leave *zero* admins; (3) **hiding a button is not gating a route** — a Member reaching `/connections/new` by bookmark or Back would have filled an entire credential form before learning it 403s; (4) the **Viewer edit-clamp was defeatable** by searching the directory again after selecting a viewer; (5) `*_secret_name` was **documented** as server-owned bookkeeping (`_carry_over_secret_name_keys` says so in as many words) and **enforced nowhere**, which made it a credential-exfiltration primitive. A comment is not a control. **[#1401](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1401) was filed as the one deliberately-left-open residual and then closed the same session by [#1403](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1403)** — #1400 closed the reference-*name* half, but the credential-bearing **URI** was still freely mutable, so an Admin could redirect a stored secret (with a `connection_versions` trail). Each adapter now declares `destination_fields` per credential slot and a config change that moves one is refused unless that credential is re-supplied: to send a credential somewhere new you must already know it. **And #1403's own review made the point a sixth time.** The guard shipped with `catalog_uri` under Iceberg's *catalog* slot only — true of a SQL catalog, and wrong for a REST one, where `catalog_properties` sends the PRIMARY secret (`secret_property: token`) as a bearer **to that same URI**. On the commonest REST shape — a `secret_ref` and no `catalog_secret_name` — the catalog slot found nothing stored and waved the move straight through. All seven regression tests reached `catalog_uri` through the catalog slot, so the hole was invisible to them by construction: **a test suite that only exercises one path through a rule cannot tell you the rule is incomplete.** The same review also found an empty-string secret satisfied "you re-supplied it" while blanking the credential — a pre-existing hole, since `reauth` had carried `min_length=1` since it shipped and create/update never did.

**The testing lesson repeated three times in one session and is now a standing rule: for a concurrency or ordering bug, writing the regression test is the easy half — proving it can FAIL is the half that matters.** Three separate tests here passed against the unfixed code and were caught only by mutation-checking them: a last-admin race driven sequentially (the interleaving never occurred), a Viewer-clamp test that skipped the "set `edit`" step (so there was nothing for the un-clamp to leak), and an OIDC role-forwarding test that never entered the branch it named. Two further habits earned their keep: **verify against the running artifact** — the per-role Playwright specs and the admin role-editor were validated in a real browser against CI's exact lane (a scratch dev-bypass API + its own Vite) after two rounds of CI-only locator failures, and the `users.role` migration was applied up *and* down against real Postgres on a populated table; and **check what the code does, not what the ticket says** — `docs/site/security/overview.md` already described this model (written ahead of the build) and was wrong in one place, claiming connection `test` was Admin-only when the ADR's normative matrix puts it at Member+.

def _suite_and_check(

def test_resolves_the_version_in_effect_when_each_result_was_written(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # #1486's own motivating case: a check that reported a MEAN when a result was written, later
    # edited to MAX/MIN — the old result must not retroactively look like a literal-cell exposure.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_table_row_count_to_equal")
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0,
        expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        column="v1_column",
    )
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=2,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between",
        column="v2_column",
    )
    before_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(hours=1))
    after_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=2))

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(
        db_session, [before_edit, after_edit], {check.id: check}
    )

    assert context[before_edit.id] == ("v1_column", "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null")
    assert context[after_edit.id] == ("v2_column", "expect_column_max_to_be_between")


def test_falls_back_to_the_live_check_with_no_version_history(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # A check created before #280 shipped (or seeded directly, bypassing check_service) has no
    # check_versions rows at all — no worse off than before this function existed.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between")
    result = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0)

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(db_session, [result], {check.id: check})

    assert context[result.id] == ("LIVE_COLUMN", "expect_column_max_to_be_between")


def test_falls_back_to_the_earliest_version_when_the_result_predates_it(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # Clock skew / same-instant edge case: every version is AFTER the result's created_at. "Before
    # the first edit" is a closer approximation of history than jumping to whatever the check is
    # today.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session)
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_min_to_be_between",
        column="earliest_column",
    )
    result = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0)

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(db_session, [result], {check.id: check})

    assert context[result.id] == ("earliest_column", "expect_column_min_to_be_between")


def test_a_result_with_no_check_id_resolves_to_none() -> None:
    # Defensive: a result whose check was hard-deleted (nullable FK path, if it
    # ever exists) must not raise.
    result = Result(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        run_id=uuid.uuid4(),
        check_id=None,
        status="fail",
        created_at=_T0,
    )
    context = run_service.historical_check_context(None, [result], {})  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert context[result.id] == (None, None)

fixup: fix 3 findings from /code-review on the DMF capability probe

1. session.commit() sat outside the try/except that was supposed to
   make the probe a soft, never-failing signal -- a commit-time DB
   error would surface as an unhandled 500 on a genuinely successful
   Test/Reauth call. Split into _capability_probe_kwargs (runs the
   probe, catches its own errors) and _persist_engine_capabilities
   (commits, rolls back and swallows on its own failure).

2. audit_coverage.py's exemption rationale for POST
   /connections/{id}/test said "changes no configuration", which the
   DMF probe made false. Corrected the rationale to name what's
   written and why it stays exempt (a re-derivable diagnostic, not
   user-authored config).

3. probe_dmf opened a SECOND Snowflake engine/connection on top of the
   one test() already opened moments earlier, doubling login latency
   on every Test/Reauth click. test() now accepts an optional
   capability_probe callback run on the SAME connection; connection_
   service wires it in via _capability_probe_kwargs instead of calling
   probe_dmf separately. The standalone probe_dmf() method stays for
   any future direct caller, delegating to the same
   _probe_dmf_on_connection helper.

Full backend suite (5856 passed, 10 skipped) and frontend typecheck
green; existing DMF tests updated for the new capability_probe/
_probe_dmf_on_connection shape, one new test proving test() makes only
one create_engine call when a capability_probe is supplied.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

# CLAUDE.md — DataQ project guide for AI assistants

> Single source of truth for any Claude / AI assistant working in this repo. Read this end-to-end before touching code.

---

## 1. Project summary

**DataQ** is a single-tenant data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations (GX Core). It runs DQ checks across **5 datasources** and integrates with **3 orchestration providers**.

| Layer | Components |
|---|---|
| **Datasources (you can write checks against)** | Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, AWS S3 **and any S3-compatible store** (MinIO/Ceph/R2/Wasabi/Backblaze, via the optional `endpoint_url` — #1063), Unity Catalog (Databricks), Apache Iceberg (native `pyiceberg` read — ADR 0030) |
| **Orchestration providers (monitor + trigger only — NOT datasources)** | Azure Data Factory (ADF), Apache Airflow, dbt (ADR 0029) |
| **Backend** | FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic |
| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco editor (generic OIDC — `oidc-client-ts`) |
| **Auth / secrets** | Three-mode ladder (ADR 0032): dev-bypass (eval) · **email OTP** (IdP-less, default for the local stack — #1150) · OIDC — **now genuinely provider-neutral end-to-end** (ADR 0026 amendment): the frontend's generic `AUTH_*` contract (ADR 0028) is matched on the backend by `core.auth.OidcBearerScheme` (OIDC discovery + JWKS via `PyJWT`, any standards-compliant issuer — Azure AD validated in prod, AWS Cognito the second target) alongside the original `fastapi-azure-auth` validator; mutually exclusive per deployment. Plus PATs (`dq_live_`) for API/MCP clients. **Authorization is two axes (ADR 0033):** a stored workspace role (`admin | member | viewer`) × the per-suite `view/edit` ladder (ADR 0027) — connection mutations are Admin-only, Viewers are read-only everywhere. Secrets: Azure Key Vault / OpenBao / AWS Secrets Manager (ADR 0039) |
| **Deploy** | Azure Container Apps (API + worker + frontend; frontend is the sole public surface, api internal — ADR 0028 §5) |
| **Observability** | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
| **AI integration** | FastMCP (50 curated tools mounted at `/mcp` — 27 read-only, 18 that change state, 5 live-probe tools gated like writes; ADR 0008 + Theme 13 Tiers 1 and 2 and Tier 3A/3B, #529/#1424, + the `get_doc` curated-docs tool (#1626) and the reusable-notification-channel read tools (#1775)) — Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor |

Timeline: **8 weeks** to v1. Scope: single tenant, suite-level access sharing, Azure-hosted.

---

## 2. Architecture at a glance

See [docs/site/architecture/overview.md](docs/site/architecture/overview.md) for the full diagram (Mermaid — renders on GitHub).

```
Browser ──HTTPS──► Frontend Container App (nginx SPA, sole public ingress)
AI clients ──MCP/HTTP──► │  proxies /api + /mcp + /healthz same-origin
                         ▼
                    FastAPI (Container Apps, INTERNAL ingress) ──► PostgreSQL
                         │  │
                         │  └──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► Snowflake / ADLS / S3 / UC
                         ├──► Redis (task queue)
                         ├──► Key Vault (secrets)
                         └──► App Insights (observability)

ADF ──► Azure Monitor alert rule ──► webhook ──► POST <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf ──► (proxied) api
Airflow ──► on_success/on_failure_callback ──► POST <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow ──► (proxied) api
FastAPI ──► MS Teams / Slack / email (alerts, ResultPublisher seam)
```

---

## 3. Repo layout

Flat monorepo (decided in Week 1):

```
DataQ/
├── backend/                     # FastAPI + Celery + GX (Python, conda)
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── core/                # logging, errors, config (locked in PR 2)
│   │   ├── db/                  # SQLAlchemy models, session
│   │   ├── api/                 # FastAPI routers (versioned: /api/v1/...)
│   │   ├── services/            # business logic per domain
│   │   ├── orchestration/       # OrchestrationProvider abstraction (ADF, Airflow)
│   │   ├── datasources/         # ConnectionAdapter + CheckRunner per type; gx_runner.py (shared GX translation), flatfile.py (flat-file IO + runner + batch resolution), sql.py (shared SQL-identifier allowlist — #428)
│   │   └── mcp/                 # FastMCP tools (Week 7)
│   ├── alembic/
│   └── tests/                   # + tests/support/ (adversarial harness), tests/integration/ (end-to-end datasource runs)
├── frontend/                    # React + Vite + Ant Design (Node, pnpm)
│   ├── src/
│   └── tests/
├── docs/
│   ├── site/                    # everything PUBLISHED to the docs site (docs_dir) — guides, architecture.md, adr/, compliance/
│   └── *.md                     # internal planning docs (progress/retro/ops-log/…) — outside docs_dir, never built
├── marketing/                   # public GH Pages marketing site (index.html — the landing page); occupies the Pages ROOT, docs build one level down into site/docs/ (mkdocs.yml site_dir)
├── integrations/                # user-deployed snippets (NOT app code; e.g. Airflow DAG callback)
│   └── airflow/                 # dataq_airflow_callback.py + setup README
├── scripts/
│   └── setup.sh                 # one-command dev env bootstrap
├── context/                     # original product/roadmap context (read-only reference)
│   └── DataQ_platform_roadmap.md
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/
│   ├── pull_request_template.md
│   ├── CODEOWNERS
│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
├── docker-compose.yml
├── environment.yml              # conda env — pip section points at backend/requirements-dev.txt
├── pyproject.toml               # Black + Ruff + mypy config
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── CLAUDE.md                    # this file
└── README.md
```

**Promotion to `apps/` + `packages/`:** only if a real shared package emerges (e.g., auto-generated OpenAPI client in Week 4–5). Default flat.

---

## 4. Datasources vs orchestration — critical distinction

**Datasources** are stores you write DQ checks against:
- Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT)
- ADLS Gen2 (flat files)
- AWS S3 — and any S3-compatible store, via the connection's optional `endpoint_url` (#1063)
- Unity Catalog / Databricks
- Apache Iceberg (native `pyiceberg` read — ADR 0030; engine-registered Iceberg tables also work zero-code under the `snowflake`/`unity_catalog` connections)

**Orchestration providers** are NOT datasources. They are workflow engines whose pipelines/DAGs we observe and react to. Their *only* three responsibilities in DataQ:

1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table (separate from `runs` / `results`).
2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific event channels (webhook for both).
3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `suite_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs.

All three providers implement a single `OrchestrationProvider` interface — ADF is the reference implementation, Airflow is the second, dbt (ADR 0029) is the third (artifact-poll + HMAC callback, no host REST API). **Never hardcode ADF-only logic; always go through the abstraction.**

| Provider | Event channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADF | Azure Monitor alert → webhook | Shared secret header (Azure Monitor's only mode) | ADF REST API, 10 min |
| Airflow | DAG `on_*_callback` → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns`, 10 min |
| dbt | post-build callback → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (app-level signing key) | poll `run_results.json` artifact (adls/s3/file), 10 min |

Airflow callbacks require the user to add a snippet to their DAGs (we can't mutate them). Polling is the documented fallback.

**Anti-pattern (do not do this):** treating ADF/Airflow as a 5th/6th datasource in the connection editor, check editor, or suite model.

---

## 5. Framework choice — GX-only for v1

- **v1:** Great Expectations (GX Core) is the sole DQ framework across all datasources. Unifies result schema, suite/check model, MCP tools, and the check editor. Every v1 check is a GX **expectation** (`check.kind = 'expectation'`).
- **v1.1+:** platform-native engines are **connection-anchored** (ADR [0036](docs/site/adr/0036-connection-anchored-check-engines.md)): every datasource connection offers GX; a Snowflake connection additionally offers **DMF**, Unity Catalog offers **DQX** (DLT/streaming — GX is batch-only), a future BigQuery type offers **Dataplex**. Engine selection is **per check** (`check.engine`, default `gx`, validated against the connection's capability set; `kind` stays orthogonal to `engine`) — supersedes the earlier suite-level `engine: gx | dqx` toggle sketch. DMF is the first native build; DQX/Dataplex are trigger-gated (see the ADR §6).
- **Monitor-kind seam (do-now, Week 3):** not every monitor is a GX expectation. A `check.kind` discriminator (`expectation` in v1; `freshness | volume | schema_drift | anomaly | comparison` reserved — freshness/volume shipped post-v1 (#426/#437) and **`comparison` shipped v1.1 W3** (ADR 0015, #791–#795) and **`schema_drift` shipped v1.1 W4** (#592) and **`anomaly` shipped v1.1 W5** (#593, rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality, PRs #1117/#1119)) + numeric `metric_value` on results let v1.x auto-monitors slot in without a check/result schema rewrite. This seam is **orthogonal to the datasource seams** (`CheckRunner`, `ConnectionAdapter`): it varies by *monitor kind*, not datasource. See ADR `0012` (and `0014` for the reserved `comparison` / cross-dataset reconciliation kind) and post-v1 roadmap Theme A. Most real incidents are freshness/volume, not value-level — this is the leap from "GX runner" to DQ platform.
- **DQ-dimension axis (v1.1 W4, ADR [0038](docs/site/adr/0038-dq-dimension-classification.md)):** every check also carries a `dimension` — accuracy / completeness / consistency / integrity / timeliness / uniqueness / validity — a **third axis orthogonal to both `kind` (how the monitor works) and `engine` (what evaluates it)**. Closed vocabulary via table `CHECK`; derived by default from the check type, **stored** (so #889 aggregates in SQL and an override survives), and overridable at any time. Derivation is **deliberately partial** — `accuracy`/`integrity` are never derivable from a rule shape and custom SQL is an arbitrary predicate — so **NULL means unclassified and must render as a coverage gap**, never silently bucketed. Existing rows were backfilled (#952, §5 amended). It is the input to the asset DQ scorecard (#889), whose value is *coverage* ("this asset has no Timeliness checks") more than score.
- **Week-3 outcome (done):** the UC run path is thin behind `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` (reads the table into a GX DataFrame asset — the DQX swap-in shape), and `check.kind` + `metric_value`/`duration_ms` shipped in the one threshold migration, so the monitor-kind impls won't ripple into the suite/check/result layer later. **Amended v1.1 W6 (#1179):** the UC runner now builds **two** batches — a GX **Databricks-SQL** batch (custom SQL; since #1532 also the default for the audited ordinary expectations — pushdown, worker memory flat) and the DataFrame one (`to_be_of_type`, sampled suites, the `UC_SQL_PUSHDOWN=false` rollback). `UnexpectedRowsExpectation`'s metrics have a SqlAlchemy provider and no pandas one, so ADR 0019's UC support had never once worked in a run *or* a dry-run; it is SQL by definition and was never going to be a DQX rule, so the DQX swap-in argument is unaffected for everything it actually covers. **Standing rule (user direction, 2026-08-28): on Databricks/UC, pushdown is the DEFAULT for any new check type** — it joins `SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES` after the #1532 live-Databricks-SQL vetting; the pandas frame batch is the exception and needs a recorded reason (no GX SQL provider, dtype-vocabulary semantics, sampling). Conversion of the 14 eligible legacy frame types is #1624.

---

## 6. Working agreements (rules above feature work)

Full list (40 rules across 8 categories) lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Highlights:

### Commit & change discipline
Per-functionality workflow, in order:
1. **One functionality per commit** (where possible).
2. **Test coverage for the functionality** (unit/integration as applicable — the ≥80% CI gate, live since Week 8, covers this).
3. **Docs updated if required** (CLAUDE.md / ADR / CONTRIBUTING / user docs — whichever the change touches).
4. **Agentic code-review on the PR** — spawn `/code-review` (never an inline self-review only) and post findings to the PR as inline comments (`/code-review --comment`).
5. **Fix issues found in the same PR** where feasible.
6. **File a GitHub issue for anything deferred** — never drop a finding silently. Use `gh issue create`; the fixing PR must include `Fixes #N`.
7. **Full CI gate must pass** (lint/format/types/tests/security — see below).
8. **Squash-merge to `main`.**

### Git workflow
- **Trunk-based** with short-lived feature branches off `main`. No long-lived `develop`.
- Branch names: `feature/<desc>`, `fix/issue-<N>-<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`, `docs/<desc>`.
- `main` is protected: PR + passing CI + no force-push. (≥1 approving review is disabled during solo-dev phase; re-enable before onboarding a second contributor.)
- **Squash-merge only into `main`.**
- **Conventional commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`).

### CI/CD quality gates (block merge)
- Ruff (lint), Black `--check` (format), mypy (types), pytest (from W8), frontend lint/format/test.
- `betterleaks` secret scanning (pre-commit + CI).
- Bandit (Python SAST) + CodeQL.
- **Dependency CVE audit (CI): `pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` (full backend runtime + test surface) + `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` (frontend).** Synchronous merge gate; complements the async Dependabot layer below.
- **Python deps have one source of truth: `backend/requirements.txt`** (runtime hub) → `requirements-dev.txt` (`-r` it + test toolchain) → `environment.yml` + CI all install from it. The re-listed subsets `requirements-dev.txt` pulls are `requirements-typecheck.txt` (the typed deps mypy needs) and `requirements-tooling.txt` (Black/Ruff/mypy/Bandit/pre-commit); the `typecheck-deps-sync` check (pre-commit **and** CI `backend-lint`) keeps the mypy hook aligned. `requirements-mutation.txt` (mutmut) is **standalone — not `-r`'d by anything**, so it stays off CI's install + `pip-audit` surface (manual tool, CONTRIBUTING rule 4a). Bump a Python version in `requirements.txt` only.
- Dependabot for npm + pip + github-actions — **version updates + security alerts/updates both enabled** (alerts scan the full pip+npm dependency graph).

### Tooling (locked in Week 1, do not drift)
- **Python:** conda env (`conda create -n dataq python=3.13`) — *not* venv, *not* poetry. (3.13 since ADR 0017; was 3.11.)
- **Black** formatter (CI-enforced).
- **Ruff** lint, **mypy** types, **structlog** logging, **Pydantic Settings** config (12-factor).
- **Frontend:** Prettier + ESLint.

### Observability
- **Structured logging from Week 1.** structlog, JSON, `request_id` correlation propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX.
- **PII redaction at logger level** (failed-check sample rows may contain sensitive data).
- **App Insights exception tracking wired Week 1**, not Week 7.

### Database
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in same PR. Two-step deploys from W5 onward.
- Migration PR checklist: rollback plan + "tested up + down locally."

### Documentation
- **ADRs in `docs/site/adr/`** — one short markdown per significant decision.
- `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from clone to working dev env.

### Security cadence
- End-of-week quick scan from Week 2: vuln alerts (Dependabot alerts + CI `pip-audit`/`pnpm audit`), secret scan, OWASP spot check, Key Vault audit.
- Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy.

## 10. Critical pointers (easy to get wrong)

- **`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`.** Orchestrator pipeline executions live in `pipeline_runs`; DQ suite executions live in `runs`. They link via `triggered_by: '<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>'`.
- **`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic.** Composite key (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. Don't add an ADF-specific bindings table.
- **PII redaction at the logger level**, not at every call site. The redactor sits in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** Code that depends on a new column ships in a separate PR *after* the migration is deployed.
- **The Week-3 threshold migration already added the schema seams (done).** It landed `check.kind` (default `'expectation'`), `results.metric_value` (NUMERIC) + `duration_ms` (INT), and the severity thresholds — see ADR `0012`. `metric_value` is the SQL-aggregatable scalar a monitor measured; **don't store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`** (you can't `AVG()`/`STDDEV()` it for trends or anomaly baselines), and **don't add a second migration re-introducing these columns**.
- **Secret scanning in pre-commit AND CI.** Don't rely on one alone.
- **Azure Monitor alert setup (Week 7) needs the deployed public API URL.** Deployment must come first; coordinate Container Apps ingress with infra/security before Week 7 to avoid a deployment-day surprise.
- **MCP tool descriptions are LLM-facing, not REST-API-facing.** Write them for natural-language selection; test against the 4 canonical NL queries in the roadmap.

## 11. What NOT to do

- ❌ Don't add ADF or Airflow as a queryable datasource in the connection editor / check editor / suite model.
- ❌ Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
- ❌ Don't deepen Azure lock-in: no reading Entra/OIDC provider claims in route/service code (depend on the generic `get_current_user`), no hardcoded Azure resource names/endpoints in business logic, no Azure-only assumptions baked into container images. Azure is one impl behind each seam — see ADR [0010](docs/site/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) / [0013](docs/site/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md).
- ❌ Don't `git commit --no-verify` past hooks. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
- ❌ Don't commit `.env` files. Use `.env.example` / `.env.app.example` as the templates.
- ❌ Don't put a credential — **even a local/mock one** — in any git-tracked file (templates, `scripts/`, CI, compose). Env templates ship the secret keys **blank** with the shape in a comment; `scripts/setup.sh` generates the local-dev password into the gitignored `.env`/`.env.app` on first run. Non-secret config defaults and non-secret identifiers (db/user name) may stay populated.
- ❌ Don't drop columns in the same PR as the code change that stops using them. Two-step it.
- ❌ Don't fix bugs silently. Raise a GitHub issue, then PR with `Fixes #N`.
- ❌ **Don't dismiss a finding because it's pre-existing.** DataQ is in production — a defect that predates your change is live for users right now, so its age is irrelevant to whether it matters. Every finding ends **fixed or filed**, never "noted in a review reply" or "documented in a docstring" (CONTRIBUTING rule 3a). Concluding it is genuinely not a defect is fine, but record the determination and evidence — verified-benign is a valid outcome, unexamined is not.
- ❌ Don't batch unrelated changes into one commit. One functionality per commit.
- ❌ Don't track GX Core at "latest." Pin the version in `environment.yml` — GX v1 API has drifted across point releases.
- ❌ Don't add a dependency under a strong-copyleft or source-available license (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL/Elastic, Commons-Clause) — DataQ ships MIT (ADR [0031](docs/site/adr/0031-oss-byol-distribution-licensing.md), CONTRIBUTING rule 40); weak copyleft (LGPL/MPL) is OK with notices. Exceptions need an ADR.
- ❌ Don't use venv or poetry for backend dev. Conda only.
- ❌ Don't write the MCP layer before Week 7. The service layer must stabilise first.

Nothing AWS-side remains open. **Security-surface audit of BOTH deployments (2026-08-16, user-directed) — three fixes shipped + deployed, two filed.** Audited from the IaC and app code, then **verified against the running deployments** rather than the docs (which is what found the first one). Verified-good: single public surface both clouds, api unreachable directly (Azure 404 / AWS ALB network-denied + origin secret), ECS task public IPs inbound-blocked, RDS private+encrypted, rate limiting live and enforcing (150-burst → 429 on both), docs off in prod, webhooks HMAC/constant-time. **#1386 was live-exploitable:** the Cognito pool had `AllowAdminCreateUserOnly: false` and its hosted UI served a working signup form, while the generic-OIDC path had **no app-side allowlist** — `_upsert_user` provisions an account for any token the issuer vouches for, so the IdP's registration policy silently WAS the product's access policy: anyone on the internet could self-register into the workspace. That also dissolved the *single-tenant, workspace-trusted* premise #1118 is deliberately accepted under, turning a known internal credential-exfiltration risk into a remotely reachable one. Fixed at the IdP (`allow_admin_create_user_only`) **and** in the app (`OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`/`_DOMAINS`, checked per-request so it revokes as well as admits; empty stays open by design — fail-closed would lock a workspace out on a routine image bump — but logs `auth_oidc_no_signup_allowlist` at WARNING). **/code-review then caught the fix's own blind spot: a THIRD generic-OIDC resolver.** Unifying the two REST dependencies was not enough — `mcp/auth.py`'s `resolve_current_user` called `_upsert_user` directly, so a token the REST API 403s authenticated at `/mcp` and got all 8 tools incl. `trigger_suite_run`, breaking the invariant that file's own Azure-guest branch states out loud. **#1387:** ZERO security response headers on either cloud (repo-wide grep found none defined anywhere). The trap: nginx drops inherited `add_header` at any level declaring its own, and three locations set `Cache-Control` — including `location /`, which serves index.html — so a server-level block would have been silently absent from exactly the response that needs a CSP, while looking correct in the config. **Proven, not assumed:** removing the `location /` re-include drops index.html to 0 headers with the server-level include still present. CSP `connect-src` is a separate runtime var, NOT derived from `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` — an authority carries a path, CSP matches by path prefix, and Azure AD's token endpoint sits outside it; live AWS confirmed the same shape from the other direction (token endpoint `…auth.us-east-2.amazoncognito.com` is a DIFFERENT host from JWKS `cognito-idp…`, so Cognito needs BOTH). Image default is `https:` not empty, so a BYO upgrade can't silently break sign-in. **#1388:** CloudFront ran `CachingDisabled` on every path — a pure pass-through absorbing nothing — in front of an in-app limiter that **fails open**, i.e. the pressure most likely to hurt Redis is what disables it. Added a WAF per-IP ceiling (2000/5min) + an 8KB body cap (import path scoped out: a WAF block happens at the edge, so its false positive has no origin log at all) and extension-matched `/assets/*.<ext>` edge caching — **not** the `/assets/*` prefix, which review caught would re-collide with the SPA's own `/assets/:assetId` route (#802 class). **Deployed to both clouds on `92c97b8c`** — Azure [run 31933670333](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31933670333) + AWS [run 31933647024](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31933647024), both green. Live-verified after: headers went **0 → 6 on both** (`server:` no longer leaks the version); CSP enforcing in prod (inline script, CDN script and `http:` connect all blocked) with the app rendering and Azure AD discovery+JWKS reachable; **the exploit is dead two ways** — hosted `/signup` now 302s with no form, and `aws cognito-idp sign-up` returns `NotAuthorizedException: SignUp is not permitted for this user pool`; WAF attached with 60/60 normal requests unaffected; edge caching Miss→**Hit** on a fingerprinted asset while `/assets/<uuid>` stays uncached `text/html`, proving the collision fix. **Left open by choice:** [#1384](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1384) (CloudFront→ALB hop is cleartext — needs a custom domain + ACM; this also made the published docs' "HTTPS/TLS everywhere" claim an overclaim, now corrected) and [#1385](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1385) (ElastiCache at-rest encryption off beside an encrypted RDS; unrestricted egress from all subnets — the exfil path #1118 would use). **Azure still has no WAF equivalent and neither cloud autoscales** — both recorded in #1388.

**Shipped 2026-08-17 — the MCP tool expansion, Tier 1 AND Tier 2 complete (Theme 13, [#529](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/529), W7 stretch), taking `/mcp` from 8 tools to 30** — 16 read-only, 10 that change state, and 4 that persist nothing but open a live datasource with stored credentials (which is why they are gated like writes). **Tier 1** was five PRs ([#1413](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1413)–[#1417](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1417)) adding the whole Tier-1 read-only set — checks (`list_checks`/`get_check`/`get_check_history`), runs (`list_runs`/`get_run_results`), ops/config (`list_connections`/`list_schedules`/`list_trigger_bindings`/`get_notification_config`), and aggregates (`get_suite_performance`/`export_suite`). Every one is a thin service-layer wrapper, so **no new authz was written**: `require_permission` already composes the ADR-0027 per-suite ladder with the ADR-0033 Viewer clamp. **Tier 2** was five more ([#1418](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1418), [#1420](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1420)–[#1423](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1423)) — check mutations (`update_check`/`delete_check`/`snooze_check`/`dryrun_check`), ops mutations (`cancel_run`/`create_schedule`/`delete_schedule`/`create_trigger_binding`), and the three role-gated capabilities (`test_connection`/`import_suite`/`suggest_column_policy`). **The deliberate exclusions hold: no connection create/update/reauth, so MCP exposes NO admin-only tool at all** — every Admin-only capability in ADR 0033's matrix is a connection mutation, and a credential must never transit an LLM. A test states that as an invariant rather than leaving the empty admin sweep looking like a forgotten row.

**The RBAC ask produced the structural change worth carrying forward: the tool-surface tripwire became DATA.** `server._require_role` is the MCP twin of the FastAPI-only `core.auth.require_role` — it cannot *be* that function, but both resolve through the same `core.roles.resolve_role` and rank with the same `ROLE_RANK`, which is exactly what keeping `core/roles.py` FastAPI-free was for. More importantly, `tests/support/mcp_gates.GATES` now declares each tool's **actual** gate and four sweeps are driven off it (Viewer-denied, Member-denied, outsider-denied, and a guard that `read` tools genuinely take no `suite_id`). The old bare set of names caught a tool being *added* but not one added with the **wrong** gate — a name in the wrong comment group looks identical to a name in the right one — and it immediately caught `profile_column` filed under "read-only" while gating on `edit`. Declaring the gate means adding a row is adding a test.

**The four `/code-review` passes returned 19 findings, and almost none were crashes — they were *honesty* defects, which is the failure mode this surface has and the REST API does not.** The same shape recurred six times: a value that is literally true and misleading to a reader with no UI around it. An expired snooze returned raw reads as active suppression on the one question ("why was there no alert?") where a wrong answer is most confident. A mid-run suite's partial outcome (`3/3, worst_severity: null`) is precisely the tool's own definition of "nothing failed", asserted about a run that has barely started — the REST runs table survives it only because a "running" badge sits beside the numbers; **an LLM has no badge, it has whatever fields it is handed**. `consecutive_run_failures: 0` renders *unknown* as a fact. A null `credential_expires_at` conflated "no readable lifetime" with "never looked". `has_email_recipients` was derived from `EMAIL_TO` while delivery also needs the SMTP transport. And `get_notification_config` reported only the per-suite webhook, so the commonest deployment shape — one workspace webhook, no overrides — answered "who gets told when orders fails?" with **nobody**. Two more were the #828 class (an unvalidated filter returning `[]`, which reads as "nothing is connected"), one was a `window_days` parameter that was **entirely inert** (`_suite_performance` scores the latest run and takes no window — so it was removed, not documented: a knob that does nothing will be used and then a difference that isn't there will be explained), and one was a docstring naming state labels the code never emits (`healthy`/`degraded` vs the real `optimal`/`stable`/`critical`/`unknown`) — *check the code, not the intent*, again. One finding was a genuine crash: `export_suite`'s NUMERIC thresholds reach the JSON encoder as `Decimal`, the #1273 class exactly, which REST never sees because Pydantic is in the way. Fixing the workspace-admin gap on `list_trigger_bindings` then broke a REST test **correctly and instructively** — it authenticated as dev-bypass, which is a workspace *admin* (#741), so it had been asserting scoping about the one principal exempt from it. Every behaviour fix was mutation-checked against the unfixed code.

**Tier 2's four reviews added twenty more findings, and the same two shapes dominated.** The honesty shape again: `create_schedule(enabled=false)` returned a `next_run_at` the docstring calls "the next time it will fire", for a schedule the dispatcher filters out and never reaches — and the identical overclaim was found sitting in the already-shipped `list_schedules`, fixed here rather than filed because an assistant may see either tool and the two disagreeing is worse than either alone. `update_check`'s docstring said omissions leave things "exactly as they were", true of arguments and **false of `config`**, which is assigned wholesale — so raising `max_value` by sending `{"max_value": 100}` deletes `min_value`, saves cleanly, and reports success. And `delete_check`'s docstring claimed historical results survive; `results.check_id` is `ondelete="CASCADE"`, so a delete erases the result history, the version history and the monitor baseline. **Writing the test is what found that one** — it was written to prove the opposite.

The second shape is a **guard applied at one door and not its sibling**, which recurred five times: unbounded `cron`/`pipeline_or_dag_id`/suite `name` reaching Postgres as `StringDataRightTruncation`, and NUL screened on a suite's name but not on the checks inside its import document — all of them escaping `_service_errors`, which maps only `DataQError`, and surfacing as opaque internal failures. `import_suite` alone had three, because it is the second door to the rows `create_check` writes and inherited none of that tool's boundary validation. **The most instructive finding was against the guard itself**: a reviewer mutation-verified that removing `require_permission` from `delete_check` left the RBAC sweep *green*, because the check-taking probes fabricated a `check_id` and the tool 404'd before authz — "check not found" being in the accepted-denial vocabulary. The same hazard had already been fixed for `run_id` and was missed for `check_id`. A guard needs its own guard checked.

Verified beyond the unit tests, both tiers: every new tool was called **through the real MCP protocol** against Postgres (in-memory FastMCP client) — 30 registered, all eight Tier-2 mutations executing for real, and all four boundary cases (over-long cron, empty pipeline id, negative snooze, over-long suite name) refused by the protocol layer before reaching the driver. One finding was left open by choice: [#1419](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1419), the REST dry-run route returning an unredacted `observed_value` while every other results surface redacts it — defensible where the consumer is the author's own editor panel, so it deserves a recorded decision rather than a unilateral change. MCP's own `dryrun_check` redacts.

**Shipped 2026-08-17 — MCP Tier 3A, 30 → 38 tools ([#1424](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1424), the Tier-3 tracker filed after the #529 expansion).** Two batches, three PRs ([#1425](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1425)–[#1427](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1427)): first `update_suite` / `get_column_policy` / `set_column_policy`, then `update_schedule` / `update_trigger_binding` / `delete_trigger_binding` / `list_check_versions` / `restore_check_version`. **The split is now 18 read-only, 16 that change state, 4 live-probe** — and it is *derived from `mcp_gates.GATES`* rather than counted by hand, after the docs drifted (see below). **Tier 3 exists because #529's candidate list was stale, not exhaustive:** it was written 2026-07-04, assets/lineage/incidents shipped 2026-07-10/11, so the largest remaining group had never been evaluated. `DELETE /suites` was added as a new permanent exclusion — it cascades every run and result the suite ever produced, and unlike `delete_check` there is no lesser action to steer an assistant toward.

**Tier 3A is *coherence*, not reach: every tool closed a dead-end or an asymmetric verb pair.** `import_suite` could create a suite that **nothing could make runnable** (no target; `trigger_suite_run` fails fast without one). `suggest_column_policy` could propose a policy nothing could read back or apply. `create_schedule` + `delete_schedule` with no update meant *"pause the nightly run"* had exactly one available answer — **delete it** — discarding the cron expression needed to restore it. `create_trigger_binding` had neither delete nor disable. And every check edit was snapshotted into `check_versions` where **none of it was readable or undoable over MCP**.

**Twelve review findings across the two batches, and the pattern is now unmistakable: this surface fails by being *misleading*, and adding a tool *ages the ones next to it*.** Four already-shipped docstrings became wrong the moment these landed — `create_schedule` and `delete_schedule` still routed the reader "to the app" for the capability just added, and `update_check` claimed recreating a check was the only way to clear a field, when `restore_check_version` is now the one path that applies emptiness rather than skipping it. **Re-read the neighbours of every new tool.** Three more were the same class in new places: a NUL guard defeated by dict-merge **key shadowing** (present, and not working, which reads as covered); `update_suite` skipping the `dispatch_auto_classify` the REST route fires, so a suite made runnable over MCP captured failing samples with **no row locator**; and `create_trigger_binding`'s "already exists" being unable to distinguish a **disabled** binding, since `uq_trigger_bindings_lookup` excludes `enabled` — an assistant re-wiring after a pause would report a trigger in place that never fires. Two claims were simply false and were found by writing the test: an empty `pii_columns` does **not** clear the policy, and `identifier_column` is **not** retroactive.

**The RBAC sweep trap recurred one level deeper, and this is the transferable lesson.** `restore_check_version` takes a `version_no`, and a probe check inserted directly rather than through `check_service` has **no version rows** — so the tool raised "check version not found" *before* reaching authz, and "not found" is in the accepted-denial vocabulary, so the sweep passed **with the gate deleted**. Same shape as the `_REAL_RUN` / `_REAL_CHECK` traps, but at the level of a *related* row rather than the resource itself. Every gate in both batches was then mutation-verified by removing it and confirming the sweep goes red; one mutation additionally proved the tool *executed* for an unauthorized user (a `check_restored` log line), which is what distinguishes "fails" from "fails for the right reason".

**Verification, and one honest correction.** All tools were exercised **through the real MCP protocol** (in-memory FastMCP client against Postgres) — 38 registered, every mutation executing for real, and every boundary case (over-long cron/timezone, `limit` 0 and 500, `version_no` 0) refused at the protocol layer before reaching the driver. **Shipped 2026-08-17 — the MCP honesty pass, all 46 tools ([#1444](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1444), user-directed).** The directive: *"The UI is expected that user will know the details. But in the MCP, that is not applicable… the answers should give the limitation and mention what it cannot see clearly to the user."* The UI's **human** supplies the missing context for free — the row count, the timestamps, the "running" badge, the filter they themselves chose. An LLM has the fields it is handed and the docstring, so a tool returning literally-true values while omitting its blind spot produces a *confident wrong answer*, which is worse than an error.

**Audited all 46 against six criteria** — population (what an empty result does NOT prove) · time window · truncation (detectable from DATA, not length) · freshness · null/zero semantics · adjacent blindness. ~75 findings. **Six docstrings were not thin but FALSE:** `get_health_score` promised "a per-day trend of the score" over a per-day count of *runs* by lifecycle status (no daily score exists); `test_connection` promised a "classified failure reason" the code deliberately withholds; `snooze_check` read as a per-check mute when suppression is per **run**; `delete_check`'s cascade omitted incidents (`Incident.check_id` is CASCADE, so it erases an open one); `trigger_suite_run` said "run the orders suite on DEV" with no env parameter; `list_connections`' `consecutive_run_failures` is the **minimum** streak across suites and reads 0 unless *every* suite is failing.

**Where a limit could be a field it became one** — prose is skippable, a field the model must branch on is not: `redaction`/`redacted_columns` (REST has had them since #1115; MCP dropped them, so a masked sample was indistinguishable from an unmasked one), `results_final`, `truncated` + `oldest_in_page`/`newest_in_page`, `sampled`/`sample_row_limit` (ADLS/S3/Iceberg profile ≤100k rows, so `row_count` was the *sample* size stated as the table's), `runnable: false`, `prior_incident_id`.

**Three lessons, all from verification catching me rather than me catching the code.** (1) A rendered-catalog check found four docstrings my *source-level* scan called clean — the splices were mid-sentence, visible only in the assembled description. (2) A routing re-run then found my repair had **corrupted two descriptions**, because my duplicate detector matched adjacent identical *words* and a repeated *phrase* walked through it — and the `list_checks` corruption sat on a safety caveat. (3) The same re-run found I had **overcorrected on ordering**: five tools led with a bolded warning, pushing the "Returns…" contract below it, which makes *selection* harder without making the caveat more likely to be read. Standing shape: **summary → what it returns → caveats.** Measured effect after the fixes: the disclosures changed the answer on **12 of 15** requests and prevented four confident wrong ones.

**And the review caught the pass's own failure mode.** I had written "**this tool can only ever ADD masking**" on `set_column_policy` — a confident absolute the code does not support, since a column named as `identifier_column` is shown unless it affirmatively classifies as PII. A false safety guarantee, produced by the very exercise meant to remove them. Six findings were left open by choice and filed: #1442 (the capability half — the tools are now *honest* about having no time filter, they still have none), #1443, #1445, #1446, #1447 (over-caveating), #1448.

**Shipped 2026-08-17 — MCP Tier 3B batch 2, 42 → 46 — Tier 3B COMPLETE.** `ack_incident` / `resolve_incident` / `list_columns` / `get_near_misses`, taking the split to **23 read-only, 18 that change state, 5 live-probe**. `list_columns` joins the live-probe group rather than the reads for the `profile_column` reason exactly — it persists nothing but opens a live datasource with the stored credential — and it is the *cheap* authoring step the surface lacked: `profile_column` reads data to compute statistics when the question was only "what are the column names?", and guessing one produces a check that runs and errors. `get_near_misses` closes the loop `create_trigger_binding` opened: that tool **warns** about an env mismatch it cannot investigate, and before this the only way to see one was `psql` (#1199).

**The lifecycle docstrings carry the load here, because both verbs are about the *incident*, not the data.** Acknowledging changes nothing and does **not** stop alerts — the check still runs, still fails, still notifies — so it points at `snooze_check` for what the user probably meant. Resolving re-runs nothing and fixes nothing: if the problem is still there the next failing run opens a **new** incident (a resolved one is never reopened), so the docstring steers toward `trigger_suite_run` to confirm before declaring victory. Both refuse the closed-state transition rather than silently no-opping, which would let an assistant report an action that never happened.

**One test-harness finding worth recording:** `SuiteForbiddenError` from `load_visible_incident` names the required level ("requires 'edit' on its suite") and matched **none** of the RBAC sweep's accepted-denial vocabulary, so a correctly-denied tool failed the sweep for looking like the wrong kind of failure. Fixed by adding that exact phrase — not a loose word like "requires", since anything also matching an argument-validation message would let a gateless tool pass by failing for the wrong reason. All four gates were then mutation-verified, and all four tools exercised through the real MCP protocol (46 registered), with the over-long note refused at the schema layer before reaching the driver.

**Shipped 2026-08-17 — MCP Tier 3B batch 1, 38 → 42 ([#1424](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1424)).** Four read-only tools over the surfaces #529 never evaluated — `list_assets` / `get_asset` / `list_incidents` / `get_incident` — taking the split to **22 read-only, 16 that change state, 4 live-probe**, again derived from `mcp_gates.GATES` rather than counted. Unlike 3A this is capability, not coherence: *"is `orders` healthy?"* is an **asset** question, and answering it from suites alone means first knowing which suites target the table, which is precisely what the asset view exists to remove.

**Two scoping rules had to reach the docstrings, not just the code.** The asset rollup is **workspace-true** (ADR 0037) — `list_visible_assets` takes no user and aggregates over ALL composing suites — so a model handed the number with no caveat will describe it as covering what the caller can see; `get_asset` therefore reports `restricted_suite_count` beside the grant-filtered suite list. Incidents, by the same ADR, stay **behind suite grants**: they are itemized failure evidence, not identity, so `get_incident` is 404-no-leak. That second rule is why **`incident:view` is a new gate value** rather than `suite:view` — the tool takes an *incident* id, so the sweep must materialise a real incident on the probe suite; a fabricated id raises "incident not found", which is in the accepted-denial vocabulary, and the sweep would pass **with the gate deleted**. The same vacuous-pass shape as `_REAL_RUN` / `_REAL_CHECK` / the 3A `CheckVersion` trap, hit for the fourth time. Both new gates were mutation-verified.

**The 404-no-leak rule moved out of the HTTP layer** into `incident_service.load_visible_incident`, shared by REST and MCP. A second hand-written copy of the only thing standing between an incident's evidence and an ungranted caller is the "guard at one door and not its sibling" shape, and that divergence is invisible until it leaks. Three honesty fields exist because the raw value is true and misleading alone — `monitored` (an unmonitored asset reads as a clean bill of health), `truncated` (against the real total; `len(page) == limit` is wrong on the exact-boundary page), and `lineage.qualified_by` (an empty graph behind a failing poller must never read as "nothing feeds this table" — #828). All four were exercised **through the real MCP protocol** against Postgres, with the boundary cases refused before the driver.

**Unplanned, user-directed, shipped 2026-08-16 — the ADR [0033](docs/site/adr/0033-workspace-roles-rbac.md) workspace-roles (RBAC) track, picked up from the `v1.1 Backlog`** (umbrella [#744](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/744), now closed): **five PRs** ([#1396](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1396)–[#1400](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1400)) taking all four slices plus the [#1118](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118) class W5 had deferred *specifically* to this track. Authorization is now genuinely two axes: a stored **`users.role`** (`admin | member | viewer`) beside the per-suite `view/edit/admin/owner` ladder, both enforced on REST and MCP, both resolving **per request** — so a demotion lands on the target's next call, *including calls made with PATs they already hold*, with no token to revoke. `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` demotes to a **bootstrap seed + lockout break-glass** that only ever grants. **This closes gap G-e and the standing hole where any authenticated user — even one holding a single `view` share — could delete or re-credential the connection every suite in the workspace ran on** (⚠️ breaking for Members who managed connections; promote before upgrading, CHANGELOG carries the note). Roles are managed in **Admin → Members** behind a **last-admin guard that counts stored-role admins only** (an allowlist-resolved admin can vanish with the next deploy) under `FOR UPDATE`, with a structured audit line per change — the durable audit *table* stays ADR 0020's deferred #310.

**The reviews caught five things the design did not, and they share one shape — a rule that was stated but not enforced, or enforced in one place but not its sibling:** (1) a **third door** around the new gates — `POST /_probe/snowflake-suite` creates a Connection *and* a Suite and was ungated; the gates went on the resources' own routes and a sibling endpoint creating the same resources by another name was invisible to that reasoning; (2) the **last-admin guard was bypassable**, reading `previous` before taking the lock so a stale value skipped the check entirely and could leave *zero* admins; (3) **hiding a button is not gating a route** — a Member reaching `/connections/new` by bookmark or Back would have filled an entire credential form before learning it 403s; (4) the **Viewer edit-clamp was defeatable** by searching the directory again after selecting a viewer; (5) `*_secret_name` was **documented** as server-owned bookkeeping (`_carry_over_secret_name_keys` says so in as many words) and **enforced nowhere**, which made it a credential-exfiltration primitive. A comment is not a control. **[#1401](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1401) was filed as the one deliberately-left-open residual and then closed the same session by [#1403](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1403)** — #1400 closed the reference-*name* half, but the credential-bearing **URI** was still freely mutable, so an Admin could redirect a stored secret (with a `connection_versions` trail). Each adapter now declares `destination_fields` per credential slot and a config change that moves one is refused unless that credential is re-supplied: to send a credential somewhere new you must already know it. **And #1403's own review made the point a sixth time.** The guard shipped with `catalog_uri` under Iceberg's *catalog* slot only — true of a SQL catalog, and wrong for a REST one, where `catalog_properties` sends the PRIMARY secret (`secret_property: token`) as a bearer **to that same URI**. On the commonest REST shape — a `secret_ref` and no `catalog_secret_name` — the catalog slot found nothing stored and waved the move straight through. All seven regression tests reached `catalog_uri` through the catalog slot, so the hole was invisible to them by construction: **a test suite that only exercises one path through a rule cannot tell you the rule is incomplete.** The same review also found an empty-string secret satisfied "you re-supplied it" while blanking the credential — a pre-existing hole, since `reauth` had carried `min_length=1` since it shipped and create/update never did.

**The testing lesson repeated three times in one session and is now a standing rule: for a concurrency or ordering bug, writing the regression test is the easy half — proving it can FAIL is the half that matters.** Three separate tests here passed against the unfixed code and were caught only by mutation-checking them: a last-admin race driven sequentially (the interleaving never occurred), a Viewer-clamp test that skipped the "set `edit`" step (so there was nothing for the un-clamp to leak), and an OIDC role-forwarding test that never entered the branch it named. Two further habits earned their keep: **verify against the running artifact** — the per-role Playwright specs and the admin role-editor were validated in a real browser against CI's exact lane (a scratch dev-bypass API + its own Vite) after two rounds of CI-only locator failures, and the `users.role` migration was applied up *and* down against real Postgres on a populated table; and **check what the code does, not what the ticket says** — `docs/site/security/overview.md` already described this model (written ahead of the build) and was wrong in one place, claiming connection `test` was Admin-only when the ADR's normative matrix puts it at Member+.
